videos.script: Two people changed the same line. Bruno moved the opening time to half past six for the winter. Ana, on her own branch, added Sunday hours to the same sentence. {{same}} Git can combine almost anything on its own. Different files, different lines of one file, it simply takes both. {{both}} But here there is no right answer it can work out. Should the bakery open at half past five, or half past six? Only a person knows. {{choose}} So Git stops, marks the line with both versions, and asks you. That is a conflict. It is not an error, and it is not anybody's fault. It is Git refusing to guess. {{conflict}} This lesson is how to read those marks and settle them. {{settle}} And it is about the other way of bringing work together, rebase, which rewrites your commits on top of everybody else's so the history reads as a straight line. {{rebase}} It comes with one rule. Break it, and your colleagues will have a very confusing afternoon. {{title}}
